name: Product Navigation
purpose: Define how navigation inside an active product or module is organized within the Application Shell, while keeping product-level destinations separate from global application navigation.
problem: Without a shared product-navigation pattern, modules can create inconsistent sidebars, mix global and local destinations, misuse submenus, lose active-context clarity, or recreate global navigation inside feature workspaces.
whenToUse: When an active product contains multiple areas, pages or functions that need persistent navigation within the same product context.
When destinations require a shallow parent-child hierarchy inside a product.
When product-level navigation must remain available while feature content changes.
whenNotToUse: To switch between global products or tools.
As tabs for switching views inside the same content surface.
For transient actions, filters or modal flows.

evidence.observation: Product-level navigation with Product Item, Product Menu, Product Submenu Item, interaction states and expanded/collapsed menu variants.
Product navigation composed inside an ERP application workspace while Global Navigation remains structurally separate.

anatomy.purpose: Identify the active product or module.
Provide direct navigation to primary product destinations.
Group related destinations when hierarchy is required.
Expose secondary destinations inside an expandable group.

compositionRules: Product Navigation belongs inside the active product workspace and must remain separate from Global Navigation.
Product Navigation should contain only destinations relevant to the active product or module.
Use Product Item for direct destinations and Product Menu only when a real secondary hierarchy exists.
Product Submenu Items must belong to a parent Product Menu.
Active state represents the current destination and must remain conceptually separate from Expanded state.
Prefer the shallowest hierarchy that accurately represents the product information architecture.
contentRules: Navigation labels should represent destinations in the product information architecture rather than actions.
Labels should remain consistent for the same destination across screens of the same product.
constraints: Do not mix Global Navigation destinations with Product Navigation.
Do not create submenu items without a parent Product Menu.
Do not use Product Navigation for transient actions.
Do not use expansion state as a substitute for active state.
Do not create additional hierarchy levels without evidence or an explicit system decision.
Reuse Aurora navigation components before creating custom local navigation.
Keep Product Navigation inside the active product context.
antiPatterns: Mixing global products and local feature destinations in the same navigation level.
Creating submenu hierarchy when no meaningful hierarchy exists.
Using navigation items as action buttons such as export or submit.
Creating arbitrary deeply nested navigation levels.
Showing multiple active destinations without a documented reason.

productExamples.usage: Navigation between ERP product areas inside the application workspace.

must: Keep Product Navigation inside the active product workspace.
Separate Global Navigation from Product Navigation.
Use Product Item for direct destinations.
Use Product Menu only when secondary hierarchy exists.
Keep submenu items under their documented parent.
Preserve Active and Expanded as separate states.
should: Prefer the shallowest hierarchy that represents the product architecture correctly.
Keep labels aligned with the product information architecture.
Reuse the same navigation structure across screens of the same product.
mustNot: Mix global products with local destinations.
Use navigation items as buttons for actions.
Treat Expanded state as Active state.
Invent routing, persistence or permission rules.
Replace Aurora navigation elements with custom visually similar controls.
